biological.citation: Knockdown of ZNF233 suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma cell proliferation and tumorigenesis (PMID: 30179682)
biological.summary: ZNF233 (19q13.31; 670-aa Krüppel C2H2-type zinc finger protein) mRNA was markedly up-regulated in HCC tissues compared with matched non-tumorous liver. Its expression correlated with tumor grade, tumor stage and patient prognosis.

biological.citation: Knockdown of ZNF233 suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma cell proliferation and tumorigenesis (PMID: 30179682)
biological.summary: Overexpressing ZNF233 in SMMC-7721 cells promoted G1/S transition and accelerated cell growth. Knockdown in QGY-7701 cells suppressed proliferation in vitro and in xenograft tumors in vivo, where Ki-67-positive cells were reduced. This indicates a positive role in HCC cell growth and suggests ZNF233 as a possible biomarker and therapeutic target.

biological.citation: Integrative transcriptomic and CRISPR dependency analysis identifies hepatoblastoma-specific essential genes and actionable vulnerabilities (PMID: 42385356)
biological.summary: ZNF233 was among the genes overexpressed in hepatoblastoma tumors versus normal liver. In a single-cell deep-learning classifier separating tumor cells from hepatocytes, SHAP analysis identified it as a major contributor, so it is part of an HB-essential/tumor-identity signature. The abstract does not state whether ZNF233 itself was among the 6 genes confirmed absent or lowly expressed in the liver microenvironment.
